_comment: WHAT EACH MODEL COSTS, and the ladders the resolver walks. One place, both consumers.
This file exists for the same reason model-pins.json does, and the reason is written in that
file: two registries of truth is how the second unpinned consumer came to exist. The Rust
voice path (app/crates/richos-voice/src/hardware.rs) compiles it in with include_str!, and
the Node call path (lib/config.js) imports it. Neither re-types a number.
IT REPLACES A HARDCODED MODEL ID ON BOTH SURFACES. Until 2026-09-10 stt.rs:42 pinned
`small.en` as a compile-time constant identical on every machine, and config.js's
DEFAULT_TIER pinned `quantized` the same way. Neither asked the machine anything: a
repo-wide grep for sysctl / hw.memsize / total_memory / sysinfo across app/crates returned
nothing. The CEO put it plainly: 'WHY IS THE SHITTIEST POSSIBLE HARDWARE HARDCODED INTO
THE APP???'
EVERY NUMBER HERE WAS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN. Provenance is per-field below. Nothing in this
file is a round number somebody liked -- that is the same defect as the constant it
replaces, one level up.
THE SURPRISE, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING: at utterance length large-v3-turbo-q5_0 peaks at
858,570,752 B against small.en's 867,516,416 B. The quantized turbo is CHEAPER in memory
than the model that config.js's tier table calls the fallback for 'low-RAM hosts'. small.en
is fp16; q5_0 is 5-bit quantized. The turbo is bigger ON DISK (574,041,195 B against
487,614,201 B) and that is the figure the old constant was defended with. So memory does not
discriminate between these models on any Mac Apple ships, and the ladders below are ordered
and gated on TIME. Full derivation: docs/measurements/hardware-model-resolution-2026-09-10/.
The machine every `reference` figure below is relative to -- and the ONLY machine any of
them has been measured on. That is not a caveat to skip: it is precisely why the resolver
measures the host it is running on instead of shipping a table of machines. A reference
figure is used for exactly one thing, computing this machine's speed factor against it.
It is the CEO's own Mac.
The utterance every `referenceUtteranceSeconds` below was measured on, and the one the
live path's calibration re-synthesizes on a machine it has not seen before.
NOT COMMITTED AS AUDIO, deliberately: `say` output drifts between renders (established by
the settings rig), so a committed WAV would imply a stability it does not have. The
sentence and the command reproduce it; the sha256 identifies the render the reference
figures came from. It is the same sentence stt.rs's module docs were written from, and it
renders to the same 3.095 s they record -- an independent confirmation, not a copy.
probe.text: Rich, what is the status of the voice pipeline today?

_comment: NOT THIS RIG'S NUMBER. It is the failure point stt.rs's own module docs state, in the only
place in either repository that says what a spoken conversation may cost: 'a second of dead
air after every sentence is the difference between talking to Rich and operating him.'
The same docs state the promise as ~0.5 s, carried below as the target for the message the
user reads. A model is admitted to the live ladder only if THIS machine decodes the probe
under the ceiling.
The batch ladder's gate. A transcription that takes longer than the recording it is
transcribing is a different product -- it stops being a batch job and becomes a backlog.
1.0 is the real-time boundary, which is a physical line rather than a chosen threshold;
there is no other non-arbitrary line available and a chosen one would be the defect this
file exists to remove. The reference machine sits 21x-23x clear of it, which is the right
shape for a guard: silent on any healthy machine, loud on one that cannot cope.
Ordered BEST FIRST. The resolver takes the first entry clearing every gate.
live: ends at tiny.en because a conversation with no recognizer is not a conversation --
the bottom rung is the one that always fits. large-v3-turbo-q5_0 sits at the TOP and is
rejected on every machine measured so far (1.549 s and 1.331 s against the 1.000 s
ceiling, two load conditions). It is left there on purpose: the door opens by itself, with
no code change and no env var, on the first machine that decodes it in time. Pretending
the ladder has a rung it can reach today would be worse than recording that it does not.
batch: STOPS at large-v3-turbo-q5_0 and is never promoted above it. That is the CEO
decision page §10 ruling and this file does not reopen it: §10 put q5_0 ahead of full
turbo on post-guard WER on both corpus renders, ahead on fabrication, and ahead on the
1,050,514,080 B a new user downloads before the product works. Promoting a big machine to
full turbo would be re-deciding §10 from a rig that measured none of what §10 decided on.
large-v3-turbo appears in `models` for its costs and in NEITHER ladder. It stays
selectable by hand (--tier turbo) exactly as §10 left it.
small.en-q5_1 is in neither ladder and in no `models` row. It is the obvious extra rung
below small.en and it is the one entry in model-pins.json with a single witness and no
copy on any machine here -- its own `witness` field says so. It stays out until the bytes
can be verified.
The rung taken when the machine could NOT be measured at all -- no probe voice, no
decoder, no cache. Deliberately NOT the bottom of the ladder: the bottom rung is where a
machine goes when it has been measured and found slow, and handing tiny.en to a machine
nobody managed to time would be a silent downgrade justified by an absence of evidence.
It is small.en because that is what shipped on every machine before 2026-09-10, so it is
the one rung with field history rather than a bench figure. An unmeasured machine gets the
status quo and is TOLD that is what happened.
